title: The roadmap is a file, and the build reads it
thesis: A team's roadmap belongs in the repo as a file, and the build should fail when the code moves and the plan doesn't.

nodes.text: Plans die where nobody has to look at them: the ones kept next to the code survive, the ones kept on the wiki don't.

evidence.filled_by: last three retrospectives: checked-in plans survived, wiki plans died

nodes.text: Being in the repo keeps a plan alive but not current; it goes stale unless something ties it to the code changing.

The brief gives no figure for how stale checked-in plans got before March 2024 beyond the eleven entries. Is 'eleven stale entries' the evidence for this claim too, or is there an earlier observation?
A build check that ties the plan to releases keeps it current.

evidence.filled_by: March 2024 script: build fails when a version bumps without a plan edit; stale entries went from eleven to zero within a month

nodes.text: The usual objection is that a forced edit is a thoughtless edit. Answer it: a thoughtless edit is still visible in review, which is more than a wiki page nobody opened can say.

evidence.filled_by: the objection itself, as stated in the brief

nodes.text: The brief has no evidence on whether the forced edits were thoughtful (e.g. review comments, reverted or boilerplate plan edits). Without it, the rebuttal is argument only; should the post concede part of the objection?
Close on the rule itself, stated plainly: no version bumps without a plan edit.

evidence.filled_by: the March 2024 script's condition, restated as the rule
